response.rationale: Complex odontoma classically presents as a dense amorphous calcified mass in the posterior maxilla with associated missing/impacted teeth, matching the vignette. Cemento-ossifying fibroma is less likely due to the irregular amorphous calcification and tooth absence. Odontogenic keratocyst is typically radiolucent, not calcified.

rejected.why: Well-demarcated calcified lesion fits, but the amorphous irregular density and missing molars are more typical of odontoma; COF usually has a mixed radiolucent/radiopaque pattern without tooth absence.
Odontogenic keratocyst is a radiolucent cyst, not a dense calcified mass; the calcification and tooth absence point to odontoma.
